name: event-handling
description: A script that demonstrates various event handling techniques.

variants.javascript-no-comments: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates event handling. The script should create a button with the text "Click me". When the button is clicked, it should change its text to "Clicked!". When the mouse hovers over the button, it should change its background color to red. When the mouse leaves the button, it should change its background color back to normal. The script should not have any comments.
variants.javascript-inline-comments: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates event handling. The script should create a button with the text "Click me". When the button is clicked, it should change its text to "Clicked!". When the mouse hovers over the button, it should change its background color to red. When the mouse leaves the button, it should change its background color back to normal. The script should include inline comments to explain the logic.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates event handling. The script should create a button with the text "Click me". When the button is clicked, it should change its text to "Clicked!". When the mouse hovers over the button, it should change its background color to red. When the mouse leaves the button, it should change its background color back to normal. The script should include JSDoc comments for the main function.

testCases.test: async () => { await page.waitForSelector('button'); const button = await page.$('button'); await button.hover(); const bgColor = await button.evaluate(el => window.getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor); console.assert(bgColor === 'rgb(255, 0, 0)', 'Background color should be red on hover'); await page.mouse.move(0, 0); const normalBgColor = await button.evaluate(el => window.getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor); console.assert(normalBgColor !== 'rgb(255, 0, 0)', 'Background color should not be red after mouse leaves'); await button.click(); const text = await button.textContent(); console.assert(text === 'Clicked!', 'Button text should change to Clicked! after click'); }
